items.title: Declarations of Pecuniary Interest under the “Municipal Conflict of Interest Act”
Mary Jane Patterson, Executive Director, and Patrick Gilbride, Associate Director/Manager of Green Infrastructure Programs, REEP Green Solutions
notes:
Mary Jane Patterson, Executive Director, and Patrick Gilbride, Associate Director/Manager of Green Infrastructure Programs, REEP Green Solutions provided a presentation on REEP's impact report, which is attached to the agenda. M. J. Patterson noted a few of REEP's successes that include an abundance of community engagement such as webinars, zero waste challenges and over 1,000 students engaged. She outlined next steps for REEP which include applying for a tree nursery and continued work on energy poverty in the Region of Waterloo.

In response to the Committee, they described their community engagement with neighbourhood associations and have supported local initiatives such as de-pave projects where asphalt is removed to have more green space. They also confirmed that collaboration with local municipalities is essential for REEP's success and that they will be working with Woolwich Staff as they work to establish a tree nursery. 

The Committee acknowledged the great work of REEP Green solutions.

items.title: Strategic Focus – Responsive and Engaging Public Service
COR-ADM-23-002, Discretionary Grant Funding 2023 Granting Program Update
notes:
In response to the Committee, Craig Dyer, Commission of Corporate Services, confirmed that the amounts in report COR-ADM-23-002, Discretionary Grant Funding 2023 Granting Program Update reflect the amounts approved in the budget on February 22, 2023. He also explained that the report is meant to provide the Committee with the 2023 grant program envelopes for clarity purposes and to provide an overview of the Region’s discretionary grant policy and processes.

The Committee directed Staff to include inflationary considerations for grant funding in the 2024 budget.
